result:
This confirms this is the only `*AgentTest` file compiled/run (no other agent tests exist yet), and all other 19 tests pass. The 4 failures are intentional — they document real bugs in `ExtendedBufferedReader`.

I wrote `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/csv/ExtendedBufferedReaderAgentTest.java` with 23 tests covering initial state, peek/read/readLine semantics across EOL styles, bulk reads, mark/reset, byte-tracking with charsets, surrogate pairs, and close behavior. 4 tests fail, each exposing a genuine bug in the production code:

1. **`testReadAtEofOfEmptyInput`** — `read()`'s line-increment check excludes a previous `CR`/`LF`/`EOF` `lastChar` but forgets `UNDEFINED`, so hitting EOF on a never-read reader bumps `getLineNumber()` from 0 to 1 for a truly empty input.
2. **`testPositionDoesNotGrowOnRepeatedEofReads`** — `read()` increments `position` unconditionally, even on EOF, so `getPosition()` keeps growing forever on repeated EOF reads instead of staying at the actual character count.
3. **`testBulkReadPositionNeverDecreasesAtEof`** — `read(char[], int, int)` does `position += len`, and `len` is `-1` (EOF) when nothing was read, so `getPosition()` actually *decreases* after an EOF bulk read.
4. **`testByteTrackingDoesNotCountEofSentinel`** — single-char `read()` calls `getEncodedCharLength(current)` even when `current == EOF`, encoding the sentinel `-1` (cast to char `0xFFFF`) as a real character and spuriously inflating `getBytesRead()` by 3 bytes.
